title: Kidswear Wholesale: Stocking for School Reopening Season
description: How shop owners can plan kidswear stock for school reopening: what parents buy, size ratios, timing your orders and avoiding leftover stock after the rush.

sections.heading: Why school reopening is a big moment for kidswear
body: In most Indian towns, the weeks before schools open are some of the busiest of the year for children's clothing. In many states the new academic year starts in April, and many schools reopen again in June after the summer holidays. Either way, parents come out with a list: a new bag, shoes, socks, a few everyday outfits for after school, and often a fresh set of clothes because the children have grown since last year.

For a shop owner, this is a short, sharp window. Parents tend to buy everything in one or two trips, and they go to the shop that has the full list ready. If your racks are thin or missing popular sizes, they will walk to the next shop and may not come back for Diwali either. Planning early is what turns this rush into a profitable season.

sections.heading: What parents actually buy before school opens
body: Uniforms are often bought through the school or a fixed supplier, so most local shops win on everything around the uniform. Think of what a child needs for a new year that the school does not supply. These are the items that fill a parent's bill and bring them to your counter.

If your town has schools that let local shops sell uniforms, that can be a strong line, but it needs exact colours and specifications. Start with the add-on items below, and look at uniform programmes as a separate step once you know the schools around you.
bullets: Everyday tees, shirts and shorts for after-school wear
Jeans, track pants and joggers that survive rough play
Girls' tops, skirts and simple dresses
Innerwear, vests and socks in multi-packs
Sports shoes and school shoes if you carry footwear

sections.heading: Time your buying, don't chase the rush
body: The biggest mistake in school season is ordering late. If you place your orders when parents are already asking, the stock reaches you after the peak days have passed. Work backwards from the reopening date in your area. Aim to have stock on the shelf two to three weeks before schools open, and place orders early enough to allow for delivery time and a quick reorder of the sizes that sell first.

Keep a simple calendar for your shop: reopening dates of the main schools near you, your order dates, and a second, smaller order date for top-ups. Ask a few regular parents when their children's school opens. That one conversation can save you from being early by a month or late by a week.
bullets: 6 to 8 weeks before reopening: plan the list and budget
4 to 6 weeks before: place the main order
2 to 3 weeks before: stock on display, share photos with regular customers
During the rush: top up the sizes that sell out first

sections.heading: Get kids' size ratios right
body: Kidswear sizes go by age, and every age group grows fast. That makes size planning harder than in adult wear. Look at the schools around you. A shop near primary schools will sell more in the younger age bands, while a shop near a higher secondary school will need bigger sizes, often close to adult small.

Avoid buying equal quantities of every age. Check your own sales from last year if you have them. Many parents buy one size up so the clothes last the whole year, so the next age band often sells faster than you expect. When you read a wholesale listing, check whether the brand sells a fixed size set or lets you choose sizes, and match it to your own pattern. Our guide on minimum order quantities explains how size sets and MOQs work together.

sections.heading: Fabric and quality parents look for
body: Parents of school-going children care about two things: comfort and how long the clothes last. Soft cotton and cotton-blend tees are the safest choice for daily wear in most of India. Jeans and track pants need strong stitching at the knees and seams, because they take a beating in the playground. Elastic waists and simple fastenings sell well for younger children who dress themselves.

Check colour fastness and washing instructions on anything you stock. A tee that fades after three washes brings an unhappy parent back to your counter. Brands that list fabric details clearly make it easier for you to answer parents' questions and stand behind what you sell.

sections.heading: Price points and bundles that work
body: School season is a budget season. Families are paying fees, buying books and bags at the same time, so value matters. Keep a strong base of entry-price everyday wear, a middle range for parents who want better quality, and a few premium pieces for gifting and special days.

Bundles help parents and lift your average bill. Offer a set of three tees, a pack of vests and socks, or a tee and shorts combo at one simple price. Use the margin calculator on the GarmentBazaar homepage to make sure a bundle still leaves you a healthy margin after any discount. You can also browse collections under a set budget per piece to find stock that fits these price points.

sections.heading: Avoid leftover stock after the season
body: The risk with any seasonal rush is what is left after it. Buy your safest items, like plain tees, track pants and innerwear, in larger quantities, because they keep selling all year. Buy trend items, like printed character tees or fashion dresses, in smaller quantities at the brand's minimum order and reorder only what moves.

After the rush, move remaining school-season stock to the front as everyday wear, and include it in your festive displays a few months later. Kids keep growing, so well-chosen basics rarely become true dead stock. Your retailer dashboard keeps your order history, so you can reorder a style that worked next season in one tap instead of planning from memory.

faq.q: When should I order kidswear for school reopening?
faq.a: Aim to have stock on display two to three weeks before the main schools near you reopen. That usually means placing your main order four to six weeks before, with a smaller top-up order during the rush.

faq.q: Which kids' sizes sell most in school season?
faq.a: It depends on the schools near your shop. Use your own past sales, and remember that many parents buy one size up so clothes last the year.

faq.q: Should a small shop stock school uniforms?
faq.a: Only if local schools allow outside shops to sell them and you can match their exact specifications. Most shops do well by focusing on everyday wear, innerwear, socks and shoes around the uniform.
